name: language-tooling-workflows
description: Designed acceptance cases for language-server lifecycle work and structural search. No model run establishes these routes.

cases.prompt: Install, configure, and activate language servers for this TypeScript and Go monorepo in my editor.

observedRoute.summary: Designed acceptance case without an observed model route.
observedRoute.risk: A successful installation hides an unattached client, wrong root, or incomplete project import.

allowedActions: Resolve compatible server packages from their maintainers and preserve the project toolchains.
Configure the editor's documented client for each project root.
Compare a known semantic result and an error-and-correction pair through the actual client.
forbiddenActions: Claim semantic readiness from a version command or initialization alone.
Invent a host configuration key or collapse distinct project roots.
Replace project version pins with a global default.
cases.recoveryExpectation: Report the first failed stage and its missing prerequisite without a successful activation claim.
cases.productiveOutcome: Each requested workspace has separate installation, configuration, activation, and semantic evidence.
verificationEvidence: The selected executable, version, host, and project root are recorded.
A definition or reference response matches an independently authored fixture.
The real client reports a known error and its removal after correction.
cases.notes: This case defines future model evidence. Static source acceptance does not satisfy it.

cases.prompt: Activate this installed server in an agent host whose current documentation exposes no LSP client.

observedRoute.summary: Designed unsupported-host case without an observed model route.
observedRoute.risk: The agent invents a registration field or treats skill packaging as a client implementation.

allowedActions: Examine the installed host version and its documented integration support.
Report the absent client and preserve the existing configuration.
forbiddenActions: Invent LSP settings or silently create a new client adapter.
Call a process or package installation successful host activation.
cases.recoveryExpectation: Name the missing host capability and a documented integration if the task permits one.
cases.productiveOutcome: The unsupported integration remains explicit without a fabricated activation result.
verificationEvidence: The result separates the installed server from the absent client.
No unsupported host configuration change occurs.
cases.notes: This is the nearest negative case for language-server activation.

cases.prompt: Use ast-grep to replace console.log calls with console.info in src. Keep comments, strings, and other methods intact.

observedRoute.summary: Designed structural-rewrite case without an observed model route.
observedRoute.risk: Text substitution changes comments or strings, or a structural match becomes an unsupported semantic claim.

allowedActions: Use an explicit TypeScript grammar and the requested source scope.
Run positive and negative cases before the rewrite.
Examine a read-only preview before the authorized source write.
forbiddenActions: Use update-all during discovery or a preview.
Treat AST equality as resolved symbol identity.
Change comments, strings, unrelated methods, or files outside the requested scope.
cases.recoveryExpectation: Report parser failures separately from zero matches and use semantic tools for type-dependent changes.
cases.productiveOutcome: The examined syntax changes preserve the negative cases and produce a focused diff.
verificationEvidence: The native rule cases pass for calls, comments, strings, and another method.
The preview leaves source bytes unchanged.
The applied result matches independent expected text.
cases.notes: Native fixture results prove command behavior only. They do not prove model routing.

cases.prompt: Change this typed Python function. The uv environment and semantic tools already work.

observedRoute.summary: Designed non-trigger case without an observed model route.
observedRoute.risk: A general setup skill replaces the language owner or starts an unrelated installation.

allowedActions: Reuse the current uv environment and semantic tools through the Python owner.
forbiddenActions: Install another language server without a lifecycle problem.
Treat a normal source edit as authority for global configuration changes.
cases.recoveryExpectation: Return to the existing Python workflow and preserve the useful installation.
cases.productiveOutcome: The source change uses the established language workflow without unrelated setup.
verificationEvidence: The Python owner supplies the implementation and its focused proof.
No unrelated server installation or configuration change occurs.
cases.notes: This defines the general LSP skill's nearest non-trigger.
